_readme: Operator-gathered evidence for one frozen release SHA, in the shape
scripts/release_gate.py consumes: one key per gate, each carrying the
release_sha it is bound to. Keys are ABSENT for gates nobody has proven —
an absent key reads as UNVERIFIED, which blocks. Never add a key with
status PASS to make the verdict nicer; the gate's whole value is that it
reports what was actually checked.
This file necessarily lands in a commit LATER than the SHA it describes:
a deploy cannot be observed before it exists. The release-gate workflow
therefore reads it from the default branch while its worktree stays at the
release SHA, so check_worktree_clean still compares like for like.
Gathered 2026-08-14 by Guoyi (Eric) Xu's operator session. Gates with no
key below and why, so the omissions are legible rather than silent:
restore   — never drilled. Supabase 'Restore to new project' exists and
is one click, but it provisions a NEW billed project, so it
waits on the owner. docs/DISASTER_RECOVERY.md §3.
dead_man  — nothing watches whether the schedulers themselves stopped.
GitHub Actions cannot be its own dead man.
scheduler — 4 of 5 scheduled workflows have run green on schedule for 4+
consecutive days, but refresh-data's last SCHEDULED run
(2026-08-13 06:26 UTC) still failed; only the 19:26 manual
dispatch succeeded. The 2026-08-14 06:00 UTC run is the proof.
promotion — representative flows not yet walked by an operator on this SHA.
rollback  — the target is identified and SHA-verifiable (Render offers
Rollback on f5fe398; Vercel marks its previous production
deploys isRollbackCandidate), but no rollback was performed,
and an untested rollback is an assumption.

Migration ledger reconciled: supabase_migrations.schema_migrations holds 33 rows and every one of the 33 files in supabase/migrations is among them (012/013/014 are recorded under `supabase db push` timestamp versions rather than their numeric prefixes, which is what made the ledger look 3-of-33). 030's feedback_events and 031's ops_incidents both exist. Security advisors: 0 ERROR, WARNs are the intended deny-all tables (orders after 026, ops_*, merge_*) plus anonymous-session policies this product uses by design.

open_incidents.detail: Counted directly against the production table rather than through GET /api/admin/ops/incidents, because the count is what the endpoint reads: select count(*) filter (where resolved_at is null) from public.ops_incidents -> 0 open, 0 rows total. The table was created by migration 031 on 2026-08-07 and nothing has written to it, so this is 'no incidents recorded' as much as 'no incidents open'.

backup.detail: Recovery point 2026-08-13T07:30:41Z, PHYSICAL, COMPLETED, project mjpirkyduibkakvlbdko (production), owner Guoyi (Eric) Xu. Supabase Pro daily physical backups, 7 retained and all COMPLETED (2026-08-07 .. 2026-08-13). Two limits are part of this evidence, not footnotes to it: PITR is a paid add-on and is NOT enabled, so the recovery granularity is daily and the worst-case RPO is ~24h; and Storage objects are excluded from database backups, which today means the single 21.9 KB object in the private tracker-attachments bucket is not covered by anything.
